prompt.context: Your client is a major OEM auto manufacturer in the US. They are extremely vertically integrated, and the client has a large number of nameplates that it fears are cannibalizing their own products.
prompt.question: What do you propose they do?

clarifying_info.a: Competition is intense in each segment. The client's individual products compete against its own products and those of competitors. However, the relative competition differs for each segment.

framework: Competitive landscape: assess how competitive each segment is and whether the client is competing against itself
Customer segments and product positioning: map vehicles across attributes (price, speed, fuel efficiency, safety) using 2x2 matrices to identify overlapping models within the same segment
Cost position: evaluate whether portfolio rationalization can improve cost efficiency through scale economies

questions.prompt: How should the client analyze its portfolio of nameplates to address cannibalization?
questions.guidance: A strong answer draws 2x2 matrices across multiple vehicle attributes (speed, price, fuel efficiency, safety) to identify which models occupy the same segment. The candidate should hypothesize that the large number of nameplates may be a legacy of combining formerly independent brands. Key insight: consumers cannot differentiate overlapping models, so some models persist without optimizing company profits.

questions.prompt: What are the options for dealing with overlapping models in the same segment?
questions.guidance: Two options: (1) Kill the less profitable model/brand and retain the more profitable one. (2) Keep both models but invest in advertising and product improvements to reposition the second vehicle into a distinctly different segment. The candidate should note that option 2 faces significant brand inertia and is harder to execute. The recommended path is to keep the most profitable vehicle per segment and eliminate duplicates.

questions.prompt: What cost savings can be expected from portfolio rationalization?
questions.guidance: Fewer models with greater volume per remaining model drives scale efficiencies across purchasing, production, engineering, and advertising. The consolidation reduces complexity costs throughout the value chain.

recommendation: Eliminate duplicate nameplates competing in the same segment; retain only the most profitable model in each segment
Invest in differentiating remaining brands so each occupies a distinct and clearly communicated position in the market
risks: Brand inertia: repositioning an established model into a new segment is difficult and may not succeed
Revenue loss in the short term if eliminated models had loyal customer bases
Internal resistance from divisions associated with discontinued nameplates
next_steps: Conduct detailed segment-level profitability analysis to determine which model to retain per segment
Develop 2x2 positioning maps across key vehicle attributes to validate segment overlap
Assess advertising and product investment required to reposition any retained second models
Model cost savings from reduced complexity in purchasing, production, and engineering
